title: Quantization accuracy gating engine with layer sensitivity profiling
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a deterministic, explainable gating engine for automated accuracy validation of quantized model variants (FP8 / INT8). The engine must combine multi-granularity metrics (token-level divergence, embedding cosine drift, top-k accuracy, per-layer sensitivity heatmaps) into human-readable pass/fail decisions and reason codes. It will run as part of the quant calibration pipeline and gate model promotions to 'validated' buckets used by runtime rollouts and CI. The goal is to reduce noisy false positives from existing threshold checks and give engineers actionable triage artifacts when a quant candidate fails.
acceptance_criteria: Engine computes a composite accuracy score per candidate using configurable weighted metrics: top-k accuracy, aggregated token KL divergence, embedding cosine similarity, and layer-sensitivity delta.
Pass/fail gate returns one of: PASS, FAIL with reason code (DELTA_KL, EMBED_DRIFT, TOPK_DROP, LAYER_SENSITIVE), or CONDITIONAL_PASS with recommended fallback model variant.
Per-prompt-bucket adaptive thresholds are supported and persisted in the calibration metadata store.

For any FAIL, the engine produces a zipped artifact with failing prompts, model outputs, logits diffs, per-layer sensitivity CSV, and a minimal reproduce script stored at s3://redwood-quant-artifacts/<key>.
Integrates with CI (quant-ci) so that a failing candidate blocks merges for runtime model promotion pipelines and posts a triage message to #quant-qc with a summary card.
Unit tests covering metric calculations, threshold adaptation, and reason code assignment with >90% coverage are present in the repository.
A smoke run across 4 representative models (base-7b, chat-13b, seq-3b, rerank-1b) demonstrates expected pass/fail outputs and is recorded in the validation dashboard.
Latency of the gating engine stage is under 120s for a full candidate evaluation using cached KV replays for a standard 2k prompt set on our CI runner (non-GPU-bound profiling allowed).
plan: Design: define composite scoring formula and reason code taxonomy; finalize per-bucket adaptive threshold algorithm (Mar 1 - Mar 4).
Implementation: metric collectors (token KL, top-k accuracy, embedding cosine, per-layer sensitivity) as independent modular processors (Mar 5 - Mar 14).
Artifact generation: produce deterministic replay bundles and a minimal reproduce script for each failed candidate (Mar 10 - Mar 18).
CI integration: quant-ci step that invokes gating engine and fails pipeline on FAIL; posts triage to Slack (Mar 16 - Mar 22).
Dashboarding: add gating outcomes to validation dashboard with drilldowns and heatmaps (Mar 20 - Mar 28).
Staged rollout: start gating for FP8 candidates only for Canary group, then expand to INT8 after 2 weeks of stable runs.
progress_updates: 2026-02-23: Initial spec reviewed with Applied ML and Runtime teams. Feedback: ensure per-layer sensitivity is normalized across architectures.

2026-02-27: Chosen composite score = weighted sum(topk_acc_score, 1 - avg_token_kl, embed_cosine_score, layer_sens_penalty). Weights are configurable via calibration metadata. Prototype weights: 0.4, 0.25, 0.25, -0.1.

2026-03-02: Implemented token-level KL collector and top-k scorer. Ran baseline on base-7b FP32 vs FP8 candidate; observed delta KL distribution skewed by prompt length—added length normalization term.

2026-03-05: Added per-layer sensitivity probe: for each layer we compute mean-param-perturbation-impact using calibrated bit-flip simulations. Produces a layer-sensitivity vector and heatmap. Early runs show peak sensitivity in attention QKV layers for chat-13b.
2026-03-09: Built artifact packaging and deterministic replay script. Artifacts saved to s3://redwood-quant-artifacts/ENG-42678/ with README and minimal reproduce.sh.
2026-03-11: CI integration spike completed. quant-ci job now calls gating-engine binary; FAIL posts to #quant-qc with link to artifact and assigns triage label.

2026-03-12: Ran smoke validation across four models. Results: base-7b-FP8 PASS, chat-13b-FP8 CONDITIONAL_PASS (recommended fallback: int8-13b-quant-lite), seq-3b-INT8 FAIL (reason: TOPK_DROP + EMBED_DRIFT). Artifacts uploaded for triage.
decisions: Use composite score approach rather than single-metric thresholding to reduce false positives.
Persist per-prompt-bucket thresholds and update them with exponential moving average after a validated run (alpha=0.1).
Introduce explicit reason codes for triage: DELTA_KL, EMBED_DRIFT, TOPK_DROP, LAYER_SENSITIVE, CACHE_MISS. These are surfaced in CI and dashboards.
Conditional passes can suggest a fallback model variant to the rollout system; they do not fully block canary deployments but mark the candidate for extra monitoring.
Artifacts are stored in our S3 bucket with retention policy 90 days by default; long-term retention requires manual action from owner.
open_questions: Should the composite score be calibrated per-architecture family (e.g., decoder-only vs encoder-decoder) or maintained as a single global config?
What is the final mapped severity for each reason code when observed together (e.g., TOPK_DROP + LAYER_SENSITIVE)? We currently treat any TOPK_DROP as high severity.
Do we allow automatic rollback on production if a deployed quant variant later triggers EMBED_DRIFT alarms in monitoring?
Edge-case: how to handle stochastic models where identical seeds produce minor output shifts—should we increase token-level KL tolerance?
test_results: Smoke run summary (2026-03-12): base-7b-FP8 composite_score=0.92 PASS; chat-13b-FP8 composite_score=0.61 CONDITIONAL_PASS; seq-3b-INT8 composite_score=0.38 FAIL.
Top-k accuracy drops observed: seq-3b-INT8 avg top1 drop=6.4% (threshold=3.0%), top5 drop=4.1% (threshold=2.0%).
Embedding cosine drift: seq-3b-INT8 mean cosine=0.81 (baseline 0.94), embed score contribution reduced composite by -0.22.
Layer sensitivity: seq-3b-INT8 shows concentrated sensitivity in feedforward layers 10-12; peak layer penalty contribution = -0.12.
False positive rate estimate from retrospective run on 30 historical candidates: 7% using composite scoring vs 19% for legacy single-threshold KL check.
End-to-end gating stage runtime on CI worker: median 86s, p95 118s.
